title: lichen_ipv6_addr_to_str does not detect truncation
description:
snprintf return value is checked for encoding failure (ret < 0) but not for truncation. If ret >= buflen, output was truncated. The current code returns 0 (success) when truncation occurs.

Location:
- ipv6_addr.c:145-166 (lichen_ipv6_addr_to_str)

What goes wrong: If a caller passes a buffer smaller than documented (LICHEN_IPV6_ADDR_STR_LEN) but larger than 0, the function returns success with a truncated, potentially malformed IPv6 address string. Downstream code parsing or logging this string gets garbage.

Note: The buflen < LICHEN_IPV6_ADDR_STR_LEN check at line 137 prevents most practical cases, but the snprintf return check should be complete for defense in depth. Header doc also promises -ENOSPC on truncation.

Fix: Add check 'if (ret >= (int)buflen) { return -ENOSPC; }' after line 158.
close_reason: Already fixed — verification-close. The bead describes a snprintf-based lichen_ipv6_addr_to_str whose truncation went undetected; the current implementation (lichen/subsys/lichen/l2/ipv6_addr.c:234-270) was refactored to a manual hex loop with: BUILD_ASSERT(LICHEN_IPV6_ADDR_STR_LEN >= 40) at compile time, an early 'buflen < LICHEN_IPV6_ADDR_STR_LEN -> -EINVAL (buf[0]=0)' guard (:241-248), and a fixed-size write (39 chars + NUL) that cannot truncate when the guard passes. The header doc correctly documents -EINVAL for a too-small buffer (no stale -ENOSPC promise). The truncation contract is test-pinned in lichen/tests/pubkey_to_iid/main.c:262-300+ (canary bytes around exact-size writes, short-buffer -EINVAL + empty-termination, canaries intact) — suite passes. The defense-in-depth snprintf check the bead asked for has no snprintf to guard; nothing to add. Tests: pubkey_to_iid host suite passes (clang/gcc builds this session).
